video.acting_natural.evidence: [Riley·claude] Muted read of the shot: I sit on the edge of the bed by lamplight. I glance back at the wall behind me, then turn to camera and chat softly about the scratches in the wall and a line someone left there. I point back at the wall once, open a hand toward the room once, and end with a quiet smile. This matches the shot's point. Beat by beat: 0–1.5s my head turns to screen left, toward the wall behind my right shoulder above the lamp, smiling with my mouth closed, which is a natural opening glance. 1.75–2.25s I turn back to face the camera, still smiling, and my mouth stays closed. 2.5–4.25s my mouth moves as I speak and my hands rest on my knees. 4.5–5.5s my right hand comes up and the thumb points back over my right shoulder toward the screen-left wall (clearest at 4.75–5.25s). By 5.75s my hand is back on my knee. The motion has a lead-in and a follow-through, and it is not stiff. 6–12s I keep talking to camera with my hands on my knees, and my head tilts and my expression shift slightly as I speak. I am never frozen like a prop, and there is no extra or exaggerated move. 12.25–13.25s my left hand opens palm-up toward the room at screen right, my eyes follow it briefly (12.5–13.0s), and at 13.25s I am already looking back at camera with the hand coming down. By 13.5s my hand is on my knee. Each gesture is used once and not repeated. 14–21.5s I say the quoted line. My mouth opens wider at about 19.5–19.75s and 21.0s, which fits stretching out the names Urbana and Vibius Restitutus. My face only goes as big as a gentle grin, never bigger than the moment. 22–23.5s I smile after the line, which fits saying 'That's kind of sweet.' 24–25.75s I go quiet and smile, and by 25.75s my head tilts down toward screen left at the lamp. That is a natural ending beat. Nothing is overplayed, nothing is done only because the script needs it, and no beat drags. The eyebrow raise (about 9–10s) is too small in the contact sheet to check, but that does not affect this verdict.
